scope_guards.gmca: Targeted field and crowdsourced measurements reflect selected locations, devices, dates and conditions; they do not guarantee current operator performance or exact-address service.
scope_guards.survey: Survey percentages describe sampled UK adults and self-reported connections or devices; they do not establish service availability for an exact household or parcel.
scope_guards.aggregate: National availability and coverage aggregates do not determine current orderability, speed or quality at an exact address.
scope_guards.consumer_rule: Consumer compensation rules apply only to qualifying customers and events under participating-provider conditions; they are not connectivity or parcel attributes.

Automatic compensation: What you need to know

dsit_facts: The DSIT Public Engagement Survey 2025/2026 was published on 16 July 2026.
95% of UK adults reported using the internet in the previous three months.
Internet use in the previous three months was 78% among adults aged 75 to 84.
Internet use in the previous three months was 46% among adults aged 85 or over.
98% of adults who used the internet had used it at home.
76% of adults felt they could complete most digital tasks without difficulty.
13% of adults aged 85 or over felt they could complete most digital tasks without difficulty.
56% of adults had improved their digital or online skills in the previous 12 months.
37% of adults reported self-teaching as a method used to learn new digital skills.
92% of adults who used the internet at home said broadband was their main connection method.
91% of all adults had connected to the internet at home using broadband or home internet.
4% of home internet users connected primarily through a Wi-Fi dongle or router using a mobile network.
31% of adults had connected to the internet at home using mobile data or a hotspot.
3% of home internet users reported mobile data or a hotspot as their primary connection method.
54% of adults who used the internet at home paid for internet or broadband by itself rather than as part of a bundle.
The survey defined standard broadband as a download speed below 30 Mbit/s.
The survey defined superfast broadband as a download speed from 30 Mbit/s to 300 Mbit/s.
The survey defined ultrafast broadband as a download speed of 300 Mbit/s or higher.
49% of adults with a broadband connection reported using superfast broadband.
19% of adults with a broadband connection reported using standard broadband.
18% of adults with a broadband connection reported using ultrafast broadband.
14% of adults with a broadband connection did not know their broadband speed category.
Ultrafast broadband was reported by 33% of households earning £150,000 or more per year.
39% of adults using the internet at home said their connection speed met their needs all of the time.
49% of adults using the internet at home said their connection speed met their needs most of the time.
6% of adults using the internet at home said their connection speed met their needs about half of the time.
2% of adults using the internet at home said their connection speed met their needs only a little of the time.
1% of adults using the internet at home said their connection speed met their needs none of the time.
50% of adults living comfortably financially said their connection speed met their needs all of the time.
28% of adults finding it very difficult financially said their connection speed met their needs all of the time.
93% of adults had a smartphone available for personal use.
96% of adults had at least one smartphone, laptop, tablet or desktop computer available for personal use.
connected_nations_facts: Ofcom published the Connected Nations Spring 2026 update on 13 May 2026.
The Connected Nations Spring 2026 update describes coverage and availability as of January 2026.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises in January 2026.
Full fibre was available to 82% of UK homes in January 2026.
Ofcom used a base of 30.5 million UK homes for the residential full-fibre availability figure.
An additional 1.2 million homes gained access to full fibre in the six months to January 2026.
Full-fibre take-up across residential and commercial premises increased by 1.8 million connections in six months.
Full-fibre take-up reached 12.4 million connections across all UK premises.
Full-fibre take-up represented 47% of all premises with access to full fibre.
Gigabit-capable broadband was available to 89% of UK homes in January 2026.
Gigabit-capable broadband was available to 27.1 million UK homes in January 2026.
Gigabit-capable broadband availability had been 87% in July 2025.
Gigabit-capable broadband had been available to 26.4 million UK homes in July 2025.
Ofcom estimated that 4,000 premises lacked access to affordable decent broadband.
39,000 premises could not access decent broadband from fixed-line or fixed-wireless networks.
The fixed-line or fixed-wireless decent-broadband gap had been 44,000 premises in July 2025.
Good 4G geographic coverage from all mobile network operators reached 84% of UK landmass, a three-percentage-point increase.
Predicted 4G geographic coverage from at least one mobile network operator remained at 96% of UK landmass.
compensation_facts: Ofcom's automatic compensation consumer guidance was last updated on 20 July 2026.
Delayed-repair compensation applies when a stopped service is not fully fixed after two full working days.
The automatic compensation amount for an unrepaired loss of service is £10.34 for each calendar day.
A missed engineer appointment, or cancellation with less than 24 hours' notice, attracts £32.31 compensation.
A delayed new-service start attracts £6.46 compensation for each calendar day of delay.
Unless otherwise agreed, compensation should be credited no later than 30 calendar days after the qualifying issue is resolved, terminated, missed or cancelled.
